title: Extract all zip, tar.gz and 7z archives in a folder at once
summary: Unpacks every zip, tar.gz, tar and 7z file in a folder in one go. Each archive gets its own folder named after it. A folder that already exists is skipped, so nothing is overwritten. A dry run shows what would happen first.

steps.expect: Lines such as: would extract: alpha.zip -> DIR/alpha/, or skip, folder exists.

steps.explain: Extract the archives. Upper-case extensions such as .ZIP work too.

prerequisites: The commands unzip, tar and 7z are installed
The archives are in one folder
warnings: Extract archives only from sources you trust; an archive can contain unexpected paths.
The script skips a folder that already exists, so a second run does nothing new.

script.content:
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Extract every .zip, .tar.gz, .tgz, .tar and .7z archive in one folder.
# Each archive goes into its own folder named after the archive (without extension).
# Existing folders are skipped, so nothing is overwritten. Upper-case extensions work too.
# Usage: extract-all-archives.sh [--dry-run] DIR
set -euo pipefail

dry=0
if [ "${1:-}" = "--dry-run" ]; then
  dry=1
  shift
fi
dir="${1:?usage: $0 [--dry-run] DIR}"
[ -d "$dir" ] || { echo "not a folder: $dir" >&2; exit 1; }

shopt -s nullglob nocaseglob
for archive in "$dir"/*.zip "$dir"/*.tar.gz "$dir"/*.tgz "$dir"/*.tar "$dir"/*.7z; do
  name="$(basename "$archive")"
  base="${name%.*}"
  base="${base%.tar}"
  out="$dir/$base"
  if [ -e "$out" ]; then
    echo "skip, folder exists: $name -> $out"
    continue
  fi
  if [ "$dry" -eq 1 ]; then
    echo "would extract: $name -> $out/"
    continue
  fi
  mkdir -p -- "$out"
  case "${name,,}" in
    *.zip)         unzip -q -- "$archive" -d "$out" ;;
    *.tar.gz|*.tgz) tar -xzf "$archive" -C "$out" ;;
    *.tar)         tar -xf "$archive" -C "$out" ;;
    *.7z)          7z x -y -o"$out" -- "$archive" >/dev/null ;;
  esac
  echo "extracted: $name -> $out/"
done
